meta.scope: Taiwan Batch 9 — Military, navy and defence-industrial statistical and recurring-citation nodes. Focuses on official defence budget, National Defense Report, indigenous naval shipbuilding (Tuo Chiang-class, Indigenous Defense Submarine), US arms-sales backlog / FMS statistics, and the defence-industrial edge into the semiconductor and economic-security clusters. Explicit referenced_by lists for force-layout strength.
meta.strategy_note: User request to press on the military and navy side. Nodes are limited to official statistical products, recurring policy reports and arms-transfer series that meet the locked definition; pure order-of-battle detail is kept secondary to citable statistical and budgetary series.

candidates.title: National Defense Budget (Ministry of National Defense)
candidates.description: Annual and special defence budget figures, including the headline MND allocation and the broader NATO-standard measure that incorporates veterans’ payments and coast-guard expenditure. Recent budgets have been set with a target of at least 3 % of GDP; the 2026 figure reaches approximately 3.32 % under the broader measure, with large year-on-year increases and dedicated special budgets for air and sea combat capability and asymmetric forces.
referenced_by: Fiscal and national-accounts analysis of government expenditure
candidates.notes: Core fiscal-security node. Rising share of GDP and the creation of multi-year special budgets for sea/air and asymmetric capabilities create direct edges into the broader public-finance and economic-resilience clusters.

candidates.title: National Defense Report (國防報告書)
candidates.description: Periodic official report (most recently the 2025 edition) that sets out the threat assessment, force-structure priorities, readiness posture and policy direction of the ROC Armed Forces. Continuously cited in subsequent budget, procurement and strategic documents.
referenced_by: Defence budget justifications and special-budget statutes
candidates.notes: Highest-level recurring-citation defence policy node. Functions as the strategic counterpart to the purely statistical budget series.

candidates.title: Indigenous naval shipbuilding statistics and programmes (Tuo Chiang-class corvettes, Indigenous Defense Submarine, light frigates)
candidates.publisher: Ministry of National Defense / Navy / related industrial agencies
candidates.description: Official and programme-level statistics and progress reporting on domestically built naval vessels — Tuo Chiang-class catamaran corvettes (multiple hulls commissioned or under construction), the Indigenous Defense Submarine (IDS / Hai Kun class) sea trials and follow-on plans, and the next-generation light-frigate programme. These programmes are central to asymmetric and sea-denial capability.
referenced_by: Defence budget (military investment and special-budget lines)
Domestic industrial and employment statistics linked to shipyards
candidates.notes: Core navy and defence-industrial node. Domestic construction of corvettes and submarines creates edges into the broader industrial base and into the asymmetric-warfare priority that now dominates procurement rhetoric.

candidates.title: Coast Guard–Navy wartime linkage statistics (Anping-class / missile stockpiles)
candidates.description: Statistical and programme information on the dual-use Anping-class patrol vessels (based on the Tuo Chiang design) and the Navy’s stockpiling of Hsiung Feng anti-ship missiles for wartime fit-out of Coast Guard hulls. Illustrates the grey-zone to high-intensity continuum in maritime force structure.
referenced_by: Defence budget and munitions stockpile lines
Maritime domain awareness and grey-zone analysis
candidates.notes: Distinctive Taiwan feature: Coast Guard hulls designed for rapid wartime conversion. Strengthens the navy–asymmetric cluster.

candidates.title: US Foreign Military Sales / arms-sale notifications and backlog to Taiwan
candidates.publisher: US Department of State / Defense Security Cooperation Agency / Congressional notifications (tracked in Taiwan and US official and analytical series)
candidates.description: Statistical tracking of notified and backlog US arms sales to Taiwan (recent packages measured in tens of billions of dollars, with a rising share of asymmetric capabilities). Forms the quantitative backbone of the security dimension of the unofficial relationship.
referenced_by: National Defense Report and procurement planning
candidates.notes: High-authority external security node. Directly links the military cluster to the US–Taiwan economic-security architecture already captured in Batch 8.

candidates.title: Domestic defence-industry and military-investment statistics
candidates.publisher: Ministry of National Defense / Ministry of Economic Affairs related / Armaments Bureau
candidates.description: Statistics and programme reporting on domestic defence production, military investment expenditure, and the industrial base that supports indigenous shipbuilding, missiles, and other systems. Interacts with the broader manufacturing and high-tech industrial statistics.
referenced_by: Industrial production and employment in related sectors
candidates.notes: Industrial edge of the military cluster. Creates potential links into the semiconductor and advanced-manufacturing nodes where dual-use technologies overlap.

candidates.title: Special budgets for asymmetric force and defence resilience
candidates.publisher: Ministry of National Defense / Executive Yuan / Legislative Yuan
candidates.description: Multi-year special budget instruments dedicated to asymmetric capabilities, munitions stockpiles, C4ISR resilience, and whole-of-society defence resilience. Distinct from the regular annual defence budget and explicitly framed as responses to the current threat environment.
referenced_by: Economic and social resilience special statutes
candidates.notes: Policy and fiscal node that operationalises the shift toward asymmetric and resilient force design. High citation value in contemporary strategic analysis.

candidates.title: Military personnel and manpower statistics
candidates.description: Statistics on active-duty strength, reserve forces, conscription/volunteer mix and related manpower indicators. Interacts with broader demographic and labour-force trends under ultra-low fertility.
candidates.notes: Links the military cluster to the demographic extremes already mapped (ultra-low fertility, super-aged society).

candidates.title: SIPRI arms-transfer statistics for Taiwan (imports)
candidates.publisher: Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI) — widely cited in official and analytical Taiwan security literature
candidates.description: SIPRI’s quantitative series on major arms imports by Taiwan. Recent five-year periods show a substantial increase, driven by the perceived threat environment and by US FMS packages. Continuously referenced in comparative security analysis.
referenced_by: National Defense Report and procurement planning
candidates.notes: International statistical counterpart to the US FMS series. Provides the long-run quantitative measure of external arms dependence.

candidates.title: Taiwan military–navy–defence-industrial cluster (meta-node)
candidates.publisher: Derived from MND, Navy, Coast Guard, US FMS and SIPRI sources
candidates.description: Meta-node that binds defence budget, National Defense Report, indigenous naval shipbuilding, Coast Guard–Navy linkage, US arms-sales backlog, domestic defence industry, asymmetric special budgets, manpower and arms-transfer statistics into a coherent security cluster that sits alongside the semiconductor and US–Taiwan economic-security architecture.
referenced_by: All detailed military and navy nodes in this batch
US–Taiwan ART / investment MOU / economic-security nodes (Batch 8)
Semiconductor and dual-use technology nodes where relevant
candidates.notes: Integrating node so the force layout can treat the military/navy complex as a high-mass object that interacts with both the chip-sovereignty architecture and the broader demographic and fiscal clusters.
